items.title: Bombay High Court refuses to quash defamation case against Rahul Gandhi for remarks on PM Modi
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Tuesday rejected the plea filed by Leader of Opposition (LOP) Rahul Gandhi challenging the defamation plea over his remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Justice NR Borkar passed the order on a plea filed by Gandhi seeking quashing of the order issuing summons. "In absence of any manifest illegality, perversity in the impugned order, it is not a fit case for interference in exercise of inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 of the CrPC. Considering the overall facts and circumstances, this Court finds no infirmity in the impugned order," the judge held. He granted Gandhi six weeks of relief from appearing before the magistrate court, giving him time to challenge the ruling in the Supreme Court. Justice NR Borkar The defamation case was filed by BJP member Mahesh Shrishrimal before the Girgaon Magistrate Court. The allegation by complainant was that in September 2018, Gandhi had conducted a rally in Rajasthan and made defamatory statements against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Due to the defamatory statement, Modi was allegedly trolled on media by various news channels and social media platforms. In August 2019, the magistrate summoned Gandhi to court

items.title: A Fundamental Right
